domain_setting: A welcoming, varied townscape with clear building silhouettes, street-level scenes and civic services. Use familiar but non-region-specific architecture so the place vocabulary is easy to distinguish.
recurring_scale_anchors: Use 304×192 scenes; make a single building or streetscape the central cue and keep people small where useful.
Contrast settlement scales: village is small and low-rise, town has a compact civic center, city has a broader skyline, downtown is the dense central core, and neighborhood is residential.
Show street-level scenes for street and plan-view blocks only for street map; keep commercial district separate from downtown.
Distinguish bus and train terminals, tourist information desk and tourist office, town hall and government building, and the distinct retail/food venues.
Use respectful, recognizable architecture for religious buildings and quiet treatment for cemetery; avoid caricature, text and numerals.
For repeated venue terms, use different scene framing: exterior storefront, interior service counter, or broad facility as appropriate.

polysemy_resolution_table.city: A large urban area with dense buildings and a broad skyline; distinguish from the smaller town and the central downtown district.
polysemy_resolution_table.commercial district: A cluster of offices and retail premises along active streets; distinguish from the taller central downtown core.
polysemy_resolution_table.downtown: The busy central area of a city with tall buildings and street traffic; not a direction or small shopping lane.
polysemy_resolution_table.historic quarter: A compact older part of town with heritage buildings, a narrow lane and traditional details; not a modern commercial block.
polysemy_resolution_table.neighborhood: A residential local area with homes, local shops and neighbors; distinct from a whole town or city.
polysemy_resolution_table.street: A public roadway with sidewalks and buildings along it; distinguish from a street map.
polysemy_resolution_table.street map: A plan view of labeled-free intersecting streets and blocks; not a street-level scene.
polysemy_resolution_table.town: A modest settlement with a central street and several civic/commercial buildings; smaller than a city and larger than a village.
polysemy_resolution_table.town square: An open public plaza at the center of town, often with benches or a fountain; distinct from a street.
polysemy_resolution_table.village: A small settlement with a few homes and a compact community setting; smaller than a town.
polysemy_resolution_table.airport: A passenger terminal and aircraft at an airfield; not merely an airplane in flight.
polysemy_resolution_table.bridge: A structure carrying a road or path over water or a lower route; show its span and supports.
polysemy_resolution_table.bus station: A terminal with multiple bus bays and waiting area; distinguish from a train station platform.
polysemy_resolution_table.gas station: A roadside fuel forecourt with pumps and canopy; use the regional synonym petrol station without confusing it with a garage.
polysemy_resolution_table.hotel: A place for overnight guests with entrance, rooms and luggage; not a private house.
polysemy_resolution_table.train station: A railway platform and station building with a passenger train; distinguish from a bus terminal.
polysemy_resolution_table.bank: A financial-services building with secure vault or counter cues; not a river bank.
polysemy_resolution_table.fire station: A municipal base for fire engines with a wide vehicle bay; no emergency in progress.
polysemy_resolution_table.government building: A public administration building with a formal civic entrance; distinguish from a town hall.
polysemy_resolution_table.hospital: A healthcare facility; use a calm exterior or treatment cue, not distress.
polysemy_resolution_table.law court: A courthouse or courtroom for legal proceedings; not a sports court.
polysemy_resolution_table.library: A public place to borrow and read books, with shelves and a service desk.
polysemy_resolution_table.pharmacy: A place dispensing medicines, shown with shelves/counter; not the academic field of pharmacy.
polysemy_resolution_table.police station: A local public safety station with a desk or station-house facade; no arrest scene.
polysemy_resolution_table.post office: A public service counter for mailing letters and parcels; no readable signage.
polysemy_resolution_table.school: An education building with classroom windows and a safe entrance; distinguish from a gym.
polysemy_resolution_table.town hall: A town’s local civic meeting and administration building, perhaps with clock or assembly entrance.
polysemy_resolution_table.tourist information: An information desk or kiosk with a map for visitors; show the service point, not an entire office building.
polysemy_resolution_table.tourist office: A small visitor-services office building with a map display; distinguish from the information desk itself.
polysemy_resolution_table.bar (pub): A public-house interior or entrance with bar counter and taps; not a sports crossbar.
polysemy_resolution_table.café: A relaxed sit-down cafe with coffee and a few tables; distinguish from quick-service coffee shop and full restaurant.
polysemy_resolution_table.coffee shop: A small counter serving coffee and light food, perhaps takeaway cups; not a sit-down restaurant.
polysemy_resolution_table.grocery store: A food shop with produce and grocery shelves; distinct from a department store.
polysemy_resolution_table.nightclub: An evening venue with dance floor, DJ booth and colored lights; no alcohol-focused or unsafe scene.
polysemy_resolution_table.restaurant: A full-service place for meals with diners, tables and a serving area.
polysemy_resolution_table.shop: A small retail storefront with a focused display window.
polysemy_resolution_table.shopping mall: A large indoor retail complex with multiple storefronts and a shared corridor.
polysemy_resolution_table.store: A larger general retail store with broad aisles or a shopping cart; distinguish from a single small shop.
polysemy_resolution_table.castle: A fortified historic residence with walls and towers; not a modern hotel.
polysemy_resolution_table.cemetery: A quiet, respectful burial ground with a few headstones and trees; no frightening imagery.
polysemy_resolution_table.church: A Christian worship building with a steeple or cross, depicted respectfully and without text.
polysemy_resolution_table.movie theater / cinema (also used in the: A cinema venue for films with a screen or ticket entrance; distinguish from live stage theater.
polysemy_resolution_table.concert hall: A purpose-built music performance venue with audience seating and stage acoustics.
polysemy_resolution_table.fountain: A decorative public water feature in a plaza; not a natural spring.
polysemy_resolution_table.leisure center: A broad community recreation facility that may include pool, gym or classes; broader than one sports court.
polysemy_resolution_table.mosque: A Muslim place of worship with a dome or minaret, treated respectfully and without readable text.
polysemy_resolution_table.museum: A public collection venue with displayed artifacts or sculpture; distinguish from a government office.
polysemy_resolution_table.park (recreation area): A public green recreational area with paths and trees; not a car park.
polysemy_resolution_table.sports center: An indoor sports facility focused on courts or training halls; distinguish from a broader leisure center.
polysemy_resolution_table.swimming pool: A facility with a clear swimming basin and water; not a hot tub.
polysemy_resolution_table.synagogue: A Jewish place of worship with a respectful architectural cue, such as a Star of David on a facade, and no text.
polysemy_resolution_table.temple: A religious worship building in the culture-course sense, with respectful temple architecture; not the body part.
polysemy_resolution_table.theater: A live stage venue with curtain, stage and performers; distinguish from a movie theater.
polysemy_resolution_table.factory: An industrial production building with loading bay or smokestacks; avoid pollution as the only cue.
polysemy_resolution_table.office building: A modern workplace building with regular windows and offices; not necessarily a skyscraper.
polysemy_resolution_table.skyscraper: An exceptionally tall high-rise tower rising above surrounding buildings; distinguish from an ordinary office block.

existing_asset_triage.lesson_72: Scanned all 3,562 keyed source SVGs. Contact-sheet reviewed 29 exact-key candidates across 25 terms; keep 23 clear contextual matches, replace wrong/weak street, park, sports-bar and table-only restaurant scenes, and select one of duplicate city/library candidates. No exact-key candidates for the remaining terms.

batch_plan: movie theater / cinema (also used in the u.s.)
glossary_context_notes: Bank is the financial institution, not riverbank. Bar is a pub, not a sports bar/crossbar. Temple is a worship building in this chapter, not the anatomical body part.

Town venues and their stored exact-match candidates were visually compared in the Lesson 72 candidate contact sheet at work/vocab-art/review/lesson-72-candidates.png. The accepted sources and replacements are enumerated in existing_asset_triage.

Batch 1 retained the clear exact city, downtown and neighborhood illustrations; commercial district is a medium-rise mix of offices and stores; historic quarter uses traditional timber/stone facades and an arch, revised after full-size review.

Batch 2 replaced the map-like street candidate with a ground-level road and retained the exact plan-view street map. Town is a compact civic center, town square an open fountain plaza, and village a small cottage cluster in greenery.

Batch 3 retained the clear aircraft terminal, fuel pumps under a canopy and hotel with luggage; bridge is a structural span and arch over a river; bus station shows multiple buses under a terminal canopy, unlike a rail platform.

Batch 4 retained the clear railway platform/train, vault-style financial bank and hospital interior; fire station is marked by its engine bay and parked engine; government building uses a broad columned civic facade, separate from the smaller town hall.

Batch 5 retained the clear courtroom, library and pharmacy scenes. Police station uses a parked patrol car and police-star badge (the first cross badge was replaced after visual review); post office uses a mailing counter, parcel and red post box.

Batch 6 kept the direct school and pub matches. Town hall is a compact clock-front civic hall, separate from the columned government building; tourist information is an outdoor visitor-map kiosk, while tourist office is a staffed-service storefront with travel brochures and a globe emblem.

Batch 7 kept the café with a relaxed storefront and the restaurant with diners; the new coffee shop focuses on espresso takeaway service, the grocery on fresh food and shopping basket, and the nightclub on dancing, stage lighting and a reflective disco ball.

Batch 8 retained the clear small-shop storefront and general-store shopping cart. Shopping mall is an indoor multi-level atrium; castle uses defended walls and crenellated towers; cemetery is a quiet burial ground with headstones and flowers.

Batch 9 reused the clear cinema facade with patrons; church uses a steeple and stained glass; concert hall shows piano and auditorium acoustics; fountain is a built tiered water feature in a plaza; leisure center shows several community activities rather than one court.

Batch 10 reused the clear museum and indoor pool images; mosque has a dome and slender minarets; park is a landscaped public garden (expanded after visual review); sports center focuses on an indoor court, while the leisure center shows multiple activity options.

Batch 11 retained the live-curtain theater candidate; synagogue is marked respectfully with a Star of David window; temple uses a traditional sweeping-eave hall; factory shows production and shipped goods; office building is a moderate mid-rise with a regular workplace window grid. Factory default-fill artifact was removed after full-size review.

Live Lesson 72 shows bank in “Public services, education, and banking” and temple in “Culture, religion, and recreation”; artwork follows those chapter-group senses (financial institution and worship building) even though the source JA glosses conflict.
